verdict.line: You lose if you let Sett stack Grit and land Facebreaker with you boxed in; you win if you kite with Q and E and starve his Haymaker shield.

brief.thesis: Sett has no dash and no ranged poke, so his entire game plan is forcing you into melee range with E (Facebreaker) and chip damage to fuel W (Haymaker). Gnar's Q (Boomerang Throw) and E (Hop) exist to deny exactly that, and the 52.6% win rate over 247 games reflects a lane where spacing, not all-in power, decides trades.

theirWindow.when: Grit bar full and E off cooldown
theirWindow.what: He will walk up for E (Facebreaker) to stun and dump a shielded Haymaker. Back off wave or trade cooldowns before his E (16/14.5/13/11.5/10s) comes off cooldown rather than standing in range when his Grit bar peaks.

yourWindow.what: Walk up and poke with Q (Boomerang Throw) or autos empowered by W (Hyper). With no dash to punish you, this is a free damage window until his E resets.

ranged poke outscales his Grit sustain

start.why: 54.5% win rate over 213 games and the higher pick rate; the extra sustain and early auto damage matter since you'll be trading autos at range before he closes in.

boots.why: 86.8% pick rate and the stronger win rate (52.4% over 250 games); Sett's autos and Q (Knuckle Down) bonus are both physical, and the flat reduction blunts his poke.

core.why: Core item in both top build paths; the move speed and damage proc both help you kite and punish his lack of gap close.
Follows Trinity in all three listed build paths; shred helps you win extended trades once he commits to melee range.
Best-performing third item (57.9% over 57 games); the health and tenacity cushion his Facebreaker stun-into-Haymaker combo.

he is building tanky and you need sustained DPS instead of burst

runes.keystoneWhy: Pairs with the 55.1% win-rate page and rewards the poke-and-reposition pattern this lane demands; master-tier Gnar players instead run Lethal Tempo (60.3% over 1,803 games) if you plan to stand and trade autos through his Grit regen rather than kite.

summoners.why: 68.4% pick rate and the highest win rate (52.7%) of the three listed options; Teleport lets you reset after kiting a Facebreaker all-in without losing wave presence, which matters since Sett has no way to punish a Teleport recall himself.

playing.title: Track his Grit bar, not his HP
playing.detail: W (Haymaker) autocasts Grit from damage taken; a full bar means a shield is coming. Back off before he hits 100% rather than reacting after the punch lands.

playing.title: Punish empty-handed Sett
playing.detail: With his E (Facebreaker) on its 16-10s cooldown, he has no stun and no gap close. Walk up and land Q (Boomerang Throw) or trade autos freely in that window.

playing.title: Never stand between two walls
playing.detail: His E (Facebreaker) pulls enemies from opposite sides into the middle, stunning only if you're pinned between himself and something else like a wave or wall. Stand on open ground so it only slows you.

playing.title: Catch your boomerang
playing.detail: Q's cooldown drops when you catch the returning boomerang; position so it flies back through you after every cast to keep up constant poke pressure.

playing.title: Save E for his all-in, not for chasing
playing.detail: Hop's cooldown (22 down to 12s) is too long to waste on minor repositioning. Hold it to disengage the moment he commits Facebreaker or ults.

playing.title: Respect R only near walls
playing.detail: His ult slams you down and deals bonus damage if you hit a wall, but he's stuck without it until level 6 and it's 120-80s cooldown. Fight away from lane walls after he's used it once.

playing.title: Transform timing wins trades
playing.detail: Once you're near max Rage, bait his next engage so you transform into Mega Gnar mid-fight; the free stun from W (Wallop) swings an even trade into a kill.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and all win-rate/pick-rate figures are pulled from measured OP.GG games on the current patch (16.20.1); the mechanical reasoning and trade-pattern advice are my own analysis layered on top.

stats.opponentTip: Be careful of having [E] interrupted with (E). Manage your distance well to kite him and gain control over lane.
